findings.summary: recover_signed_intent never calls read_recovery_directive; current recovery returns Ok and quarantines, while the integration test still expects Err then terminal Aborted. A test-only expectation change cannot establish terminal abort.

Only daemon startup holds SingleInstanceLock and daemon RPC/tick mutex; Supervisor public recovery and raw Fleet mutation APIs do not carry an owner capability. The single-file lifecycle CAS does not serialize the complete abort snapshot.

Intent write validates a current same-grant constraint then atomically replaces; no protected compare of exact current intent digest at commit. Directive write is separately exported and unguarded. Atomic file replacement alone does not make a multi-file state check atomic.

The non-exact adopted Matrix recovery branch calls kill then removes lease/drops handle without observed exit. Absence of runtime/lease after this branch cannot satisfy the safe-abort no-live-process premise.

Do not unconditionally add Aborted to early terminal statuses: the ordinary daemon gate reads only production_recovery_required while explicit Start and lower start_release_slot do not independently check unresolved release transactions. Internal target startup must remain distinct from explicit Start.
